http_edges/host_header_odd.cite: actionpack-6.1.7.10 lib/action_dispatch/middleware/host_authorization.rb:96-101, `DefaultResponseApp#response_body`: `return "" unless request.get_header("action_dispatch.show_detailed_exceptions")`.  The class comment at :17-19 states it: "The body of the response contains debug info if +config.consider_all_requests_local+ is set to true, otherwise the body is empty."  actionpack-6.0.6.1's DEFAULT_RESPONSE_APP (:77-88) has no such branch.
http_edges/host_header_odd.why: Rails 6.1 changed what `ActionDispatch::HostAuthorization` puts in the body of the 403 it answers a request with an unrecognised `Host` header.  6.0's default response app always rendered the `rescues/blocked_host` debug template, so the recorded body carried the "Action Controller: Exception caught" title, its two headings and the "Blocked host: evil.example.com" text; 6.1's returns an empty body unless the request has `action_dispatch.show_detailed_exceptions`, which production does not.  The status is 403 on both, which is the requirement step 05 introduced and this step keeps -- what moved is how much the refusal says to the caller, and it says less, which is the direction the change was made in.

Ruby 3.0 release notes: "Arguments delegation known as `def foo(...)` ... keyword arguments are separated from positional arguments."

migrate/migrate.up.why:
Two changes in one recorded stream, both in the lines `rake db:migrate` prints for the application's own migrations, and neither touching the schema they produce -- `pkdrift` reads the same 7 tables before and after and agrees.
  (1) Eleven `add_column`/`change_column` lines lose a trailing `{}`.  `Migration#method_missing` logs `arguments.map(&:inspect)`, and the compatibility layer these migrations run under declares `add_column(table, column, type, **options)` and calls `super`.  On Ruby 2.7 an empty `**options` still arrived at `method_missing(*arguments)` as a positional `{}`; on Ruby 3.0, with keyword arguments separated, it arrives as nothing at all.  This one is the interpreter's, not the framework's -- the logging code is character for character the same in 6.0 and 6.1.
  (2) One `add_reference` line gains `:_uses_legacy_reference_index_name=>true`.  That is the framework's: 6.1 adds a `V6_0` compatibility layer below `Current`, and every migration declared for an older release now inherits from it, so the flag 6.1 uses to keep pre-6.1 index naming is set on the options hash before the line is logged.

subscriptions/notify.after_answers.cite: actionview-6.1.7.10 lib/action_view/log_subscriber.rb:92-93, `log_rendering_start` opening with `debug do`; actionview-6.0.6.1's same method at :85-86 opens with `info do`.  Rails 6.1 release notes, Action View: the render-start and partial-render log lines move to the debug level.
subscriptions/notify.after_answers.why: Action View 6.1 logs the line it prints when a template starts rendering at `debug` where 6.0 logged it at `info`.  The mail world records this application's own log at info, so the "  Rendering notification_mailer/weekly_activity.html.erb" line that opened the recorded stream is gone and the "  Rendered ... (Duration: | Allocations:)" line that closed it is now first.  Three lines become two; no mail changes.  The companion `*_mail` cases still record the envelope, the recipients and the parts, and spec/mailers/notification_mailer_spec.rb still asserts the recipient, so nothing about what was delivered stops being checked -- exactly the argument step 05 made when the same three cases flipped for the mailer's own log line.
